rule: FL-M5 T12 query encoder for the Cloud Run API: which ONNX graph ships; committed before `onnx_embedder check` runs on any graph
decided: 2026-11-26 (user chose bge-base ONNX int8 in the image, subject to this check)
split: ret-dev (182 queries) only; the test split is not used: retrieval quality was settled in FL-M3, this checks that the new encoder reproduces it
fl_m3_source: bench/embed_queries_dev.json (exact recall@10, bge-base fp16 GPU query vectors vs the stored corpus vectors)

pipeline_check.measure: lowest cosine between the ONNX fp32 CPU query vectors and FL-M3's stored dev query vectors
pipeline_check.basis: FL-M3's own fp16-GPU vs fp32-CPU check gave a lowest cosine of 0.9999995 (bench/embed_corpus.json); an fp32 graph below 0.999 means the pipeline differs (tokenizer, instruction, pooling), not precision

int8_accept.measure: 0.2967 minus the int8 graph's exact recall@10 on the same 182 queries and stored corpus vectors
int8_accept.basis: one query is 1/182 = 0.0055 of recall@10, so 0.01 allows at most 1 query to lose its relevant chunk from the top 10; also requires the pipeline check to pass

ship: int8 if int8_accept holds; else opt-fp32 if the pipeline check holds (image size then checked in T12e against 0.5 GB); else nothing ships and the export is fixed first
reported_not_thresholded: same exact top-10 sets vs FL-M3's query vectors (of 182)
lowest cosine of the int8 vectors vs FL-M3's
max |CLS| difference vs torch fp32 on 8 queries
latency per query on 1 CPU thread (p50 / p95, tokenization included)
